title: NIST CSF 2.0 AI System Profile: Mapping the Six Functions to AI Governance — Council of AI Compliance Guide
context: 2026-08-31 engine cycle — NIST released the Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 in February 2024 with the new Govern function; the AI system profile, expected Q3 2026, maps all six CSF functions to AI-specific risks including model poisoning, prompt injection, data provenance, and supply-chain integrity. The Council of AI verified measurement credential provides a machine-readable, Ed25519-signed artifact that slots into the CSF's Recover and Respond functions as continuous monitoring evidence.
body: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (CSF 2.0) introduced a structural change that matters enormously for AI governance: the Govern function (GV) now sits at the centre of the framework, establishing cybersecurity risk management as a board-level concern rather than an IT-operations afterthought. For organisations deploying AI systems — particularly general-purpose AI models, high-risk classifiers under the EU AI Act, or systems processing personally identifiable information — the CSF 2.0 AI System Profile (expected final publication Q3 2026) provides a subcategory-by-subcategory mapping that bridges cybersecurity controls to AI-specific failure modes. The six-function structure works as follows for AI systems. Govern (GV): the organisation's AI risk management policy must name accountability for model safety, data provenance, and third-party model supply-chain risk. The Council of AI verified measurement credential serves here as an auditable policy artifact — a signed statement that a model was measured against the 14-axis board on a specific date, with specific results, by a specific verifier. Identify (ID): asset management expands to include model registries, training data inventories, and fine-tuning lineage. A CSF-conformant AI asset inventory must record the model version, its training cut-off date, the provenance of any fine-tuning data, and the cryptographic hash of the model weights at deployment time. Protect (PR): access controls extend to model serving endpoints, prompt APIs, and embedding stores. Rate-limiting, input filtering, and output scanning are Protect subcategory controls; the Council of AI containment index — a signed, append-only incident log — provides evidence that protective controls are active and monitored. Detect (DE): continuous monitoring for AI systems includes drift detection (distribution shift between training and inference data), adversarial prompt detection, jailbreak attempt logging, and anomalous output pattern detection. The Detect function is where the measurement board's detector-interoperability axis becomes operational: a model's refusal rate, jailbreak susceptibility, and content-safety boundary must be measured continuously, not at a single point-in-time. Respond (RS): when a detection fires — a zero-day jailbreak vector, a data-exfiltration incident via prompt injection, or a model behaving outside its safety envelope — the Respond function requires incident response specific to AI. The containment index records the incident, its severity, and the remediation applied, with each entry signed and append-only. Recover (RC): post-incident, the model must be re-measured against the full board before returning to production. The verified measurement credential is re-issued post-recovery, providing auditable evidence that the recovery was effective. The practical integration path is: map each CSF subcategory to an AI-specific control, instrument the control with a measurement point, and record the measurement in a signed, verifiable artifact. Organisations subject to both CSF 2.0 and EU AI Act Article 15 (accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity) can use a single measurement-credential architecture for both frameworks. The Council of AI alignment: the verified measurement credential is a CSF-compatible continuous-monitoring artifact that is independently verifiable by any third party holding the published public key — no trust in the provider required, only cryptographic verification.
